rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (670.5, best) finishes the oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20). The slalom still fails 20/20 off track at progress 0.3144, which is identical to iteration 3 and nearly identical to iterations 4 to 6 (0.30 to 0.35). Progress has not moved across changes to kp (2.6 to 3.0), kd, base_speed (1.0 to 0.85), sensor reach (y 0.05 to 0.07) and array width. That points to a fixed failure point on the slalom, not a gain or speed problem. Slalom line_loss_events fell to 0.2 in iteration 7, so the robot is not losing the line often. It is leaving the 0.06 m band on a sharp bend while still near the tape. Untested levers are sensor footprint and line-loss search behaviour. Change (only one): sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m. A larger footprint gives more tape coverage per sensor, so the signal stays valid through sharp bends and the robot keeps a graded error rather than a sharp drop. Everything else is kept at iteration 7 (kp 2.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 0.85, wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.6, seven sensors at y 0.07 from x -0.08 to 0.08, weights x/0.04, last_direction line loss), so the effect is isolated. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.4 with fewer off-track ends, and oval and s-bend finish rates at or above iteration 7. Risk: a larger footprint blurs the centre estimate on the oval, so if oval max_error rises above 0.025 I will revert to 0.012. Hypotheses for the next race: (a) if slalom progress stays near 0.31, the failure is a geometric or search limit, so I will test line_loss search_right; (b) if slalom line_loss_events rise, the footprint overlaps the background too much; (c) if the oval completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, raise base_speed to 0.95. Measurements requested: all names in the observation list, so that per-track progress, max_error and line-loss events can be compared with iteration 7.
